scope: Native window identity, ownership, selection, focus, lifecycle, saved-view and watch-list projection. Native capability gaps remain explicit; this does not complete the entire Excel window API or Medium stage. No independent pane/view or platform window service is added.

required_obligations.profile: Native monotonically allocated window IDs; live insertion-order global/workbook collections, captions, one-based workbook-relative Index/WindowNumber, xlWorkbook Type, selected sheets, active sheet/cell and native multi-area range selections. Targeted reads restore focus. Explicit Activate and new windows retain focus; next/previous use the visible native list. Caption is read-only. SaveChanges is ignored for non-last windows. Last-window Close uses the existing workbook lifecycle with callbacks, prompts and Boolean completion. Deleted windows fail 91. Native parked active sheets follow session sheet identity across rename/reorder. Read-only window scopes also restore inactive workbooks’ live view without changing activation recency. Dynamic roots follow the currently shown native/UI window. Application collections are session-owned and survive closing a different originating workbook. User cancellation of a Close prompt returns False. If a close callback or paused prompt adds a sibling, commit closes only the original window and preserves the workbook.

Bounded native CustomViews stash captures sheet ordinal, selection, sheet zoom and sheet freeze. Add requires explicit PrintSettings=False and RowColSettings=False; defaults and True refuse before effects. Names are read-only and duplicate names refuse. Show validates stored metadata and protected selection before commands. Native snapshot uses sheet positions, not a persisted worksheet lifetime; changing workbook sheet topology can invalidate its meaning. Any collection edit invalidates all prior CustomView handles via the stash defined-name lifetime; callers reacquire them. Native XLSX preserves the stash. These snapshots do not add independent per-window view settings.

Application.Watches aggregates native per-document lists in workbook/list order. Add accepts a single-cell same-session Range, stores qualified native cell text, checks destination trust, and returns the existing handle on duplicate source. Source returns a Range only for a qualified single-cell source; legacy relative/malformed UI entries refuse rather than retarget. Native text references do not track sheet rename/deletion. Any watch-list edit invalidates prior handles in that document; reacquire them. Delete-all validates all destination permissions before effects. Uses existing native watch command and undo-preservation behavior; no new watch codec/event source.

Existing Application.Goto with Scroll=False works on the active native window. Existing single-window Scroll=True retains its worksheet-saved top-left behavior. With two windows on the same workbook Scroll=True refuses before selection/history effects because native scroll storage is sheet-owned. Independent Window/Panes zoom, freeze/split, scrolling, display flags and display modes are out of scope until native per-window state exists. No substitute single Pane or inferred viewport is returned. Geometry, pixel transforms, VisibleRange and arrangement need a real window/viewport host service on both native and browser; headless never fabricates measurements. SheetViews and dialog/module/TreeviewControl graphs, ScrollArea restrictions, synchronized side-by-side state and Office Creator identity have no native backend. Caption assignment and native missing per-window activation events are unsupported.
